title: Coaching and mentoring factsheet
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Coaching and mentoring as development through one-to-one conversations; coaching as a skilled, non-directive activity; mentoring as a longer relationship with a more experienced colleague; line managers as coaches and the power issue; check readiness; set confidentiality and information-flow rules between coachee, coach, manager and HR; coaching supervision as quality assurance. Visible date 11 Aug 2025 (metadata also shows 29 Dec 2022).

title: Global Code of Ethics for coaches, mentors and supervisors
publisher: Global Code of Ethics (EMCC Global, Association for Coaching and 10 other bodies)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A guidance document, not legally binding; first published 2016; Version 4 (2025) updated December 2025; signed by 12 bodies including EMCC Global, the Association for Coaching and APECS; separate guidance on technology and AI. The code text itself is a download and was not read.

title: The effects of feedback interventions on performance: a historical review, a meta-analysis, and a preliminary feedback intervention theory (Kluger and DeNisi, Psychological Bulletin 119(2), 1996)
publisher: Hebrew University of Jerusalem research portal
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 607 effect sizes from 23,663 observations; average d = .41; over one third of feedback interventions decreased performance; feedback works less well as attention moves from the task to the self.

title: Performance management: could do better? (evidence review)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 6 Dec 2016. Specific, challenging goals work for simple tasks, less for complex ones; feedback is needed for goals to work; whether people see appraisal as fair and useful matters; keep development conversations separate from pay and promotion decisions.

title: Closing the gap between intent vs. impact: the SBII feedback model
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Situation-Behavior-Impact feedback (situation, observable behaviour, impact) and the added Intent step that asks what the person was trying to do. Published 19 Aug 2025.

title: The feedback equation (Lara Hogan, 2018)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Observation, impact, then a genuine question or a request; choose the impact the recipient cares about; people jump to requests too fast. First published 15 July 2018.

title: Our approach: Radical Candor
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Two dimensions (care personally, challenge directly), four quadrants (radical candor, ruinous empathy, obnoxious aggression, manipulative insincerity) described as behaviours, not personality types; order: ask for feedback, give specific praise, then kind and clear criticism.

title: Coaching as a developmental intervention in organisations: a systematic review of its effectiveness and the mechanisms underlying it (Grover and Furnham, PLOS ONE, 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Coaching benefits organisations but evidence is thin (small samples, self-report, retrospective designs); client readiness and the relationship as factors; internal vs external coach evidence weak. Reports Theeboom et al. effect sizes (.43 coping to .74 self-regulation; performance .60, .19 after removing one study) and Jones et al. (.26 skills, .46 affective, 1.15 individual-level). The original meta-analyses blocked fetching.

title: Does mentoring matter? A multidisciplinary meta-analysis comparing mentored and non-mentored individuals (Eby, Allen, Evans, Ng and DuBois, Journal of Vocational Behavior 72(2), 2008)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (Europe PMC record with abstract; the PMC and PubMed pages showed a browser check). Mentoring linked to better outcomes across behaviour, attitudes, health, relationships, motivation and career; effects generally small; workplace and academic mentoring larger than youth mentoring.

title: EMCC Global
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Began in 1992 as the European Mentoring Centre, renamed EMCC Global in 2023; not-for-profit registered in Belgium; accreditation for coaches, mentors, supervisors, team coaches and programmes; links the Global Code of Ethics.

title: 1-1 (GitLab Handbook)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; body text read from the handbook's public source file on gitlab.com. The 1-1 belongs to the direct report; private shared agenda doc filled 24 hours ahead; at least weekly with at least two live 1-1s a month; manager talks about 20% of the time; fallback questions; monthly career conversations. Undated.

title: State of the Global Workplace (2026 report, 2025 data)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Global engagement 20% in 2025; manager engagement 22%, down from 27% in 2024; many managers lack coaching training; 263,810 respondents (141,444 employed) in 2025.

title: Where to get urgent help for mental health
supports: Opened with WebFetch. NHS 111 (mental health option) or online; 999 or A&E if life is at risk; Samaritans 116 123. Last reviewed 23 Oct 2026.

title: Find NHS Talking Therapies for anxiety and depression
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Adults in England can refer themselves without a diagnosis; covers anxiety, depression and related problems. Last reviewed 14 Feb 2025.

title: Help for mental illnesses
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Call 911 in a life-threatening situation; call or text 988 in distress; FindTreatment.gov; start with a primary care provider. Last reviewed April 2026.

title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Call or text 988 or chat online; free, confidential, 24/7.

title: Management Standards for work-related stress
supports: Opened with WebFetch. HSE's Management Standards approach to work-related stress, with a preparation stage and five steps. Last updated 13 Jan 2025.

title: Supporting mental health at work
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Managers should check in regularly and act early without assuming; agree adjustments with the worker; employers must make reasonable adjustments for disabled workers and must not discriminate. Last updated 16 Jan 2025.

title: Harassment
supports: Opened with WebFetch. What makes harassment unlawful; employer liability for supervisors and co-workers; 180-day deadline to file a charge, which state law may extend.

title: AI Act: regulatory framework for AI
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Emotion recognition in workplaces and education banned from 2 Feb 2025; AI for employment and worker management is high-risk, with duties from 2 Dec 2027 after the AI Omnibus (in force 27 Jul 2026). Page updated 19 Oct 2026.

title: NIMHANS: Tele MANAS services

supports: Opened with WebFetch. Lists Tele-MANAS, India's National Tele Mental Health Programme, on 14416 and 1800 891 4416. Official India source for mental health help; the Tele-MANAS site itself failed a certificate check.

title: 9-8-8: Suicide Crisis Helpline

title: Mental health: psychological health and safety

title: Mental health helplines
